**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` resource requires SSH access to the node when creating and uploading a cloud-init snippet.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to reduce usage of SSH for provisioning resources, thus I propose to use the https://github.com/kdomanski/iso9660 library to create an ISO image on the fly (basically what's happening here: https://github.com/Telmate/terraform-provider-proxmox/blob/186ec3f23bf4a62fcad35f6292fa1350b8e1183b/proxmox/resource_cloud_init_disk.go#L77-L122)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The information:
> Consider using `proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file` resource instead. [...]

On the `proxmox_virtual_environment_file` docs is good advice for downloading OS installer ISOs directly onto the node, but for cloud-init disks you usually would want to create them locally from a yaml file or inline specification.

**Additional context**
I'm happy to create a pull request for this feature, if desirable.

items.title: VM create retries after "got no worker upid" and then fails with "VM is locked (create)"
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
When Proxmox VE answers a VM create with HTTP 500 "got no worker upid", the provider sends the create again. PVE wrote the new VM's config with `lock: create` before it tried to start the worker. Nothing removes that config when the start fails. So the retry gets "VM 50201 already exists on node 'pve'". The already done check in `CreateVM` takes that for its own success. The provider then resizes the imported disk, which fails with "VM is locked (create)". The lock never clears, because the task that would remove it never ran.

The "got no worker upid" comes from a race in PVE. `fork_worker` in pve-common reads the new worker's UPID with `POSIX::read` and doesn't retry on EINTR. A SIGCHLD from another task ending at that moment fails the start. PVE tracks it as its bug 8124. I hit it in an OpenTofu module with `random_vm_ids` on, while other tasks ran on the node. The ID was free. The race is PVE's to fix. Still, a create that failed this way created nothing, and a retry under the same ID can't succeed.

The create retry counts "already exists" as success, on the assumption that the first attempt created the VM. After "got no worker upid" it hasn't.

Container create does the same. I checked `pct create` the same way: it locks the new config before it starts the worker, and the retry gets "CT 97101 already exists on node 'pve'". `CreateContainer` and `CloneContainer` use the same retry and already done check.

**To Reproduce**
Sending SIGCHLD to a pvedaemon worker right after it forks forces the race. Signals sent earlier fail the request before the create, with "Unable to load access control list".

1. On the node, as root, start this watcher. Once a pvedaemon worker forks a child, it sends that worker SIGCHLD for 20 ms:

   ```sh
   timeout 60 perl -MTime::HiRes=usleep,time -e '
       sub kids { open(my $f, "<", "/proc/$_[0]/task/$_[0]/children") or return; split " ", <$f> // "" }
       my %old = map { $_ => 1 } map { kids($_) } @ARGV;
       while (1) {
           for my $w (@ARGV) {
               next unless grep { !$old{$_} } kids($w);
               my $end = time + 0.02;
               while (time < $end) { kill "CHLD", $w; usleep 20 }
               exit;
           }
       }' $(pgrep -f '^pvedaemon worker') &
   ```

2. Within those 60 seconds, run `tofu apply` with the configuration below.
3. See the apply fail on the disk resize with "VM is locked (create)".
4. See the VM's config hold only `lock: create`: `cat /etc/pve/qemu-server/<id>.conf`. Only `qm unlock` as root clears it.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = { source = "bpg/proxmox" }
  }
}

provider "proxmox" {
  endpoint      = "https://pve.example.com:8006/"
  api_token     = "root@pam!token=<secret>"
  random_vm_ids = true
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "test" {
  node_name = "pve"
  name      = "test-no-worker"
  started   = false

  disk {
    datastore_id = "local"
    interface    = "scsi0"
    import_from  = "local:import/debian-13-genericcloud-amd64.qcow2"
    size         = 4
  }
}
```

and the output of `terraform|tofu apply`.
```text
proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.test: Creating...

Error: VM disk resize

  with proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.test,
  on main.tf line 13, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "test":
  13: resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "test" {

task
"UPID:pve:00000FA8:000287B2:6AE77F1F:resize:50201:root@pam!token:"
failed to complete with exit code: VM is locked (create)
task log:
  TASK ERROR: VM is locked (create)
```

**Expected behavior**
The apply fails on the create with the "got no worker upid" error, after one create request.

**Screenshots**
None.

**Additional context**

- Single or clustered Proxmox: single
- Proxmox version: 9.2.21
- Provider version (ideally it should be the latest version): 0.120.0, and the same code on main
- Terraform/OpenTofu version: OpenTofu 1.13.1
- OS (where you run Terraform/OpenTofu from): Debian 13
- Debug logs (`TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform apply`): the relevant lines

```text
[DEBUG] Received HTTP Response: tf_http_res_status_reason="500 got no worker upid ... start worker failed"
[WARN]  retrying VM create
[DEBUG] Received HTTP Response: tf_http_res_status_reason="500 unable to create VM 50201 ... VM 50201 already exists on node 'pve'"
```

items.title: docs: refocus README on evaluators and contributors, move known issues to the docs site
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

`README.md` tries to serve evaluators, new users, contributors and operators at once. The user-facing parts (Known Issues, version requirements, example-deployment prerequisites) duplicate the docs site or have no counterpart there, and the duplicated copies have drifted. Several claims are stale or wrong:

- "TLS 1.3 required, 1.2 optionally supported": the client accepts `min_tls` from 1.0 to 1.3, defaulting to 1.3.
- Known issue "HA VMs / containers ... the provider will report an error": both VM and container Read follow the guest to its live node; the actual outcome is a `node_name` drift that migrates back or recreates. The multi-node guide already documents this correctly with an `ignore_changes` recipe.
- Known issue "VMware disk images cannot be uploaded or imported": the file resource auto-detects `.vmdk` as `import` content on PVE with import storage, and `import_from` takes it directly. The rename-to-`.img` workaround is obsolete on PVE 9.
- Known issue "Hardware mappings cannot be created by non-PAM accounts": PVE's `/cluster/mapping/{pci,usb,dir}` create/update/delete endpoints check only `Mapping.Modify`; no root check exists. The claim came from the original 2024 implementation PR note and no issue ever reported it.
- "Compatibility Promise" heading over a paragraph that says "we will try"; `(currently 9.2)` is a hand-pinned minor that rots.
- The example-deployment prerequisite list duplicates `docs/guides/dev-proxmox-setup.md`, which is more complete.
- The fork lineage is the third sentence on the page, ahead of what the project is; upstream stopped in Feb 2021 and ~2,500 of 2,590 commits are post-fork.
- No Security section on the landing page despite two high-severity advisories in 2026 rooted in documented sudo configurations; the policy lives only in `.github/SECURITY.md`.
- No quickstart snippet; the README contains no HCL at all.
- Terraform / OpenTofu floors (1.5 / 1.6) are stated in the README, absent from the docs site, and not what CI tests (Terraform 1.6.x; OpenTofu not in CI).

### Describe the solution you'd like

Refocus the README on evaluators and contributors; move user-facing content to the docs site.

README:

- Header: title, badges, description, maintained-by, disclaimer. Lineage moves to a dated "History" line at the bottom.
- Quickstart: minimal `required_providers` + `provider` block (endpoint, api_token, no SSH) and one link to the docs.
- Compatibility: PVE 9.x tested against current 9.x, 8.x/7.x notes, 0.x paragraph, pointer to Requirements in the docs. Drop "Promise" and the minor pin.
- Security: reporting link, API-first posture, SSH/sudo caution, link to the advisories page.
- Testing and Future Work unchanged (from #3138).
- Example resources collapsed to a few lines linking the dev-setup guide.
- Known Issues removed.

Docs site:

- `docs/index.md`: new Requirements block (PVE 9.x, Terraform 1.6+ tested in CI, OpenTofu 1.6+ supported but not in CI, write-only attributes need TF 1.11 / OpenTofu 1.10, TLS 1.3 default with `min_tls`).
- New `docs/guides/known-issues.md`: HA drift (summary + link to multi-node guide), serial device on cloud-image disk resize, lock errors on parallel create, snippets need PAM + SSH, VMware images via `import_from`. Hardware-mapping root item dropped as disproven.

### Additional context

Follow-up to #3138. Decisions above were walked through with the maintainer section by section.

items.title: Support compressed disk images (e.g. `.qcow2.xz`) via API-based import_from
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `import_from` disk attribute imports images through the Proxmox **API**, so it needs no SSH access or `sudo` on the node. However, PVE's import datatype does not decompress, so compressed vendor images (e.g. Fedora CoreOS `fedora-coreos-*.qcow2.xz`) cannot be consumed by `import_from`. Users who need those images must fall back to the legacy `file_id` custom-disk import, which shells out to `qm disk import` / `qm set` over SSH and therefore requires SSH access plus a sudoers grant on the node.

This leaves compressed images as the one disk-provisioning case with no fully API-based path.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Handle compressed images without a privileged on-node command. For example, extend the download/upload pipeline (`proxmox_virtual_environment_file`) to decompress supported archive formats (`.xz`, `.gz`, `.zst`, ...) client-side before uploading a plain `.qcow2`/raw image to an import-capable storage, so it can then be attached via `import_from` entirely over the API. This would give every disk-provisioning case an SSH-free path and let deployments drop SSH from their setup where it was only needed for this.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Keep using `file_id` — works today but requires SSH + `sudo` on the node, which is exactly what we want to make optional.
- Wait for PVE to add server-side decompression to the import datatype. If/when that lands, `import_from` could consume the compressed file directly and this feature becomes unnecessary.

**Additional context**

Open questions to resolve during design:

- Where decompression runs, and its CPU/disk cost for large images.
- Required storage content types for the staged, decompressed image.
- Checksum / integrity handling for the decompressed artifact.
- Lifecycle of the staged image: cleanup, and re-use across applies.

items.title: Creating a proxmox_virtual_environment_vm whose disk uses import_from (importing a downloaded cloud image) fails on the very first apply
items.body:
Describe the bug

Creating a proxmox_virtual_environment_vm whose disk uses import_from (importing a downloaded cloud image) fails on the very first apply with:

Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply

When applying changes to proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.<name>, provider
"provider[\"registry.opentofu.org/bpg/proxmox\"]" produced an unexpected
new value: root object was present, but now absent.

This is a bug in the provider, which should be reported in the provider's
own issue tracker.

TF_LOG=DEBUG shows the actual cause: the provider unconditionally issues an internal disk resize immediately after creating a VM with an import_from disk (regardless of whether size is set on the disk block), and then verifies the VM via GET /cluster/resources?type=vm instead of the VM's own config/status endpoint. That cluster-wide resource list is only eventually consistent (populated by pvestatd's periodic poll, ~10s by default) and routinely comes back {"data":[]} for a VM created and resized only moments earlier. The provider reads the empty list as "the resource no longer exists," even though the VM was created successfully and genuinely exists — confirmed independently via GET /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/config moments after the failure, and via the Proxmox UI.

This reproduces 100% of the time in our environment, regardless of:

Target disk storage (reproduced on both Ceph RBD and local-lvm)
Whether disk.size is explicitly set to match the import size, left unset, or set to something else
Whether template = true is set at create time
Whether an agent block is present
Provider version (reproduced from 0.66 through 0.111.1)

To Reproduce

Minimal config (values redacted/generalized):

hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.111"
    }
  }
}

provider "proxmox" {
  endpoint  = var.proxmox_endpoint
  api_token = var.proxmox_api_token
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file" "cloud_image" {
  content_type = "import"
  datastore_id = "local"
  node_name    = var.target_node
  url          = "https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
  file_name    = "ubuntu-cloudinit-base.qcow2"
  overwrite    = true
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "test" {
  vm_id     = 9000
  name      = "test"
  node_name = var.target_node
  started   = false
  machine   = "q35"
  bios      = "ovmf"

  cpu    { cores = 1 }
  memory { dedicated = 1024 }

  disk {
    datastore_id = "local-lvm"
    import_from  = proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.cloud_image.id
    interface    = "virtio0"
    iothread     = true
    discard      = "on"
    # size intentionally omitted -- reproduces either way; see below
  }

  initialization {
    datastore_id = "local-lvm"
    interface    = "ide2"
  }

  network_device { bridge = "vmbr0" }
}
tofu apply
Watch it fail on proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.test with "Provider produced inconsistent result after apply / root object was present, but now absent" a few seconds after the "Still creating..." messages stop.
Check Proxmox directly (UI, or GET /nodes/{node}/qemu/9000/config) — the VM exists, with the disk correctly imported.

Expected behavior

Apply succeeds, or at minimum the provider verifies the newly-created VM via its own node/vmid endpoint (which is authoritative and immediately consistent) rather than the cluster-wide resource list (which is not).

Debug log excerpt

Two separate apply attempts, both ending the same way. First, with disk.size explicitly set to match the requested import size (20GiB, i.e. no actual size change needed):

[INFO]  Resizing disks after VM creation

items.title: fix(vm): do not drop vm from state on cluster resource list miss
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

<!--- Clearly state the problem and how this PR solves it. -->

On a multi-node cluster, creating a `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` could fail on the very first apply with `Provider produced inconsistent result after apply … Root object was present, but now absent` (#3022), and `terraform import` could fail with `Cannot import non-existent remote object` (#1878). `vmRead` located the VM through `GET /cluster/resources?type=vm` and treated a miss as "the VM is gone". That list is built from the guest list of whichever node serves the request, which on a cluster can lag behind a config file written on another node moments earlier, and Create calls Read immediately when the VM is not started. A single-node host never shows this, since the create task and the list share one pmxcfs instance, which is why the existing suite never caught it.

A cluster-list miss no longer blanks the ID. Read keeps the node from state and falls through to the authoritative `GET /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/config`, whose not-found branch still removes the VM from state. A cluster-list hit still updates `node_name`, so out-of-band migration detection (#391) is preserved. The always-true pointer-vs-string comparison on the node name is corrected as a side effect.

Two new acceptance tests run the provider through an in-test TLS reverse proxy that answers every `/cluster/resources` request with an empty list: one creates and imports a bare VM, the other mirrors the reported configuration with a downloaded cloud image imported as the boot disk and resized after create. Both fail before the fix and pass after, on a single-node host. A `WithInsecureEndpoint` render option is added to the test environment for this.

The post-create resize of `import_from` disks mentioned in the issue is by design: `disk.size` defaults to `8` and the provider resizes the imported disk to match the configuration.

**Describe the bug**
When importing an existing VM that was originally created with a disk.file_id reference (e.g., pointing to a downloaded image), the provider does not populate the file_id field during the import. As a result, a subsequent terraform plan triggers a forced replacement of the VM, even though no actual configuration has changed.

1. Create a VM using proxmox_virtual_environment_vm with a disk.file_id referring to a proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.

**Description:**
When creating a VM with the `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm` resource, Terraform repeatedly tries to update the disk configuration even though no changes were made in the configuration.

**Terraform configuration (simplified):**

```hcl

    architecture = var.base.arch
  }

    dedicated = var.resources.memory * 1024
    floating  = 0
    hugepages = var.resources.hugepg ? "any" : null
  }

  network_device {
    bridge = "vmbr0"
  }

  initialization {
    datastore_id = var.disks.cloudinit.storage
    interface    = "scsi0"

    ip_config {
      ipv4 {
        address = "${cidrhost(var.network.cidr, count.index + 2)}/${local.mask_part}"
        gateway = cidrhost(var.network.cidr, 1)
      }
    }

    user_data_file_id = proxmox_virtual_environment_file.cloudinit_pve[count.index].id
  }

  disk {
    import_from = proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.cloudinit_img.id
    interface   = "virtio0"
    size        = var.disks.root.size
    discard     = "on"
    iothread    = true

    datastore_id = var.disks.root.storage
  }

  efi_disk {
    datastore_id = "SSD"
    type = "4m"
  }

  dynamic "disk" {
    for_each = { for i, disk in var.disks.other: i => disk }

    content {
      interface    = "scsi${disk.key}"
      size         = disk.value.size
      datastore_id = disk.value.storage
    }
  }
}
```

**Observed behavior (`terraform plan`):**
Terraform reports an in-place update for an existing VM due to a `disk` block, even when nothing changed in configuration:

```
  ~ disk {
      + aio          = "io_uring"
      + backup       = true
      + cache        = "none"
      + datastore_id = "SSD"
      + discard      = "ignore"
      + interface    = "scsi0"
      + iothread     = false
      + replicate    = true
      + size         = 32
      + ssd          = false
    }
```

**Error when applying (`terraform apply`):**

```
Error: Defined disk interface not supported. Interface was , but only [ide sata scsi virtio] are supported

  with module.master_pool.proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.vm[1],
  on modules/pve_pool/main.tf line 97, in resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":
  97: resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm":
```

**Expected behavior:**

* Terraform should recognize the disk as already in the desired state and not attempt to update it unnecessarily.
* If an update is required, the provider should handle the `interface` field correctly instead of treating it as an empty string.

**Additional notes:**

* This issue occurs with both the root disk and dynamically attached disks.
* Seems like a diff bug where provider-generated defaults (`aio`, `backup`, `cache`, etc.) are not normalized against the configuration.
* Might also be related to the way `discard` is handled (`ignore` vs `on`).

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Define a VM with a root disk and optional dynamic disks as shown above.
2. Run `terraform apply` to create the VM.
3. Run `terraform plan` again without making changes.
4. Observe Terraform trying to modify the disk and failing with the error above.

items.title: fix(vm): stop re-emitting `format=` on existing `import_from` disks
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

When a VM has an existing disk created with `import_from` on file-based storage and the user adds a sibling disk in a later apply, Proxmox would silently rewrite the existing disk's stored config to add a `format=qcow2` qualifier — even though the Terraform plan only mentioned the new disk. The user-visible symptom is short orange "pending change" lines in the PVE GUI on disks the user did not touch.

Two-part fix in the SDK VM disk path:

1. **`proxmox/nodes/vms/custom_storage_device.go`** — drop `ImportFrom` from `CustomStorageDevice.Equals()`. PVE never echoes `import-from=` back in its config response (it is a one-shot import source, not persisted state), so plan-vs-API comparison is permanently asymmetric for imported disks. Comparing `ImportFrom` made every unchanged imported disk look "changed" forever, routing it through the update path on every apply.
2. **`proxmoxtf/resource/vm/disk/disk.go:Update()`** — defence in depth: when picking `tmp = currentDisks[iface]` for an existing-disk update, set `tmp.Format = nil`. `UnmarshalJSON` derives `Format` from the file extension (`.qcow2`) when PVE omits the qualifier, so leaving it set re-emits `format=qcow2` on the wire and persists it onto PVE's stored config. Mirrors the existing `tmp.Size = nil` pattern (resize has its own endpoint, so size is intentionally excluded from the update body for the same reason).

items.title: ReadResource fails fatally on missing disk instead of marking resource as tainted
items.body:
When a VM disk no longer exists in Ceph (e.g. due to a previously interrupted destroy operation), the provider fails fatally during ReadResource with HTTP 500 when attempting to read the disk. This makes it impossible to proceed with terraform plan or terraform destroy without manual state manipulation.
The provider has sufficient information to conclude that the disk no longer exists — the VM config and VM status are both readable and return HTTP 200. Instead of treating the missing disk as "resource no longer exists" and continuing, the provider aborts the entire plan with a fatal error.

# To Reproduce:
Have a VM whose disk no longer exists in Ceph (or probably any datastore) while the VM configuration still exists in Proxmox
Run terraform destroy

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "linux_vm" {
  name      = var.name
  node_name = var.node_name

  disk {
    datastore_id = "ceph-datastore"
    import_from  = "cephfs:import/debian-13-generic-amd64.qcow2"
    interface    = "virtio0"
    size         = 100
  }
}

textError: error get file klanten:vm-97854-disk-0 from datastore klanten: 
received an HTTP 500 response - Reason: rbd error: rbd: error opening image vm-97854-disk-0: (2) No such file or directory

# Expected behavior
When the provider receives HTTP 500 for a disk read during ReadResource, it should treat this as "disk no longer exists" and mark it as such in state, allowing Terraform to proceed with the destroy.
This is consistent with standard Terraform provider conventions — a "not found" response during Read should result in the resource being removed from state rather than a fatal error. If the goal of a destroy operation is to ensure a resource no longer exists, receiving confirmation that it already doesn't exist should be treated as success, not failure.

# Additional context
The debug logs show that the provider has sufficient context to make the correct decision:

VM config is readable — returns HTTP 200
GET /api2/json/nodes/node04/qemu/97854/config → 200
"virtio0": "klanten:vm-97854-disk-0,..."

VM status is readable — returns HTTP 200
GET /api2/json/nodes/node04/qemu/97854/status/current → 200
"status": "stopped"

Only the disk itself is missing — returns HTTP 500
GET /api2/json/nodes/node04/storage/klanten/content/klanten:vm-97854-disk-0 → 500
"rbd error: rbd: error opening image vm-97854-disk-0: (2) No such file or directory"

Result: entire plan fails
ERROR vertex "HUBA-webapp-01 (orphan)" error: error get file klanten:vm-97854-disk-0

# Workaround:
terraform state rm 'module.tenant.module.linux_vm["vm-01"].proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.linux_vm'
terraform destroy -parallelism=1

Clustered (3 nodes)
Proxmox version: 9.1.7
Provider version: 0.102.0
Terraform version: 1.14.8
OS: Windows

items.title: Feature Request: Improve usability of `proxmox_files` for conditional file usage
items.body:
### Description

The `proxmox_files` data source is very useful for listing files in a Proxmox datastore. However, using it in combination with `proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file` to implement a very common workflow is currently more complex than expected.

This is especially noticeable when working with cloud images (`content_type = "import"`) used as base disks for virtual machines.

---

### Problem

A frequent use case is:

> "Use an existing base image if it exists in the datastore; otherwise, download it and use it."

While the provider already offers all the necessary building blocks (`proxmox_files` and `proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file`), implementing this behavior requires a significant amount of boilerplate and manual logic.

---

### Current Workaround (Full Example)

```hcl
locals {
  target_file_name = "noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"

  matching_files = [
    for f in data.proxmox_files.images.files : f if f.name == local.target_file_name
  ]

  image_file_id = length(local.matching_files) > 0 ? local.matching_files[0].id : proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.ubuntu_image[0].id
}

data "proxmox_files" "images" {
  node_name    = "pve"
  datastore_id = "local"
  content_type = "import"
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file" "ubuntu_image" {
  count = length(local.matching_files) == 0 ? 1 : 0

  node_name    = "pve"
  datastore_id   = "local"
  content_type  = "import"

  url              = "https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
  file_name = "noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm" {
  name      = "example-vm"
  node_name = "pve"

  disk {
    datastore_id = "local"
    file_id      = local.image_file_id
  }
}
```

---

### Why this is problematic

For such a common workflow, the current approach requires:

* Manual iteration and filtering over `files`
* Multiple `locals` variables
* Conditional resource creation using `count`
* Conditional selection of IDs
* Handling Terraform indexing (`[0]`)

This increases complexity and reduces readability.

---

### Proposed Improvement

Improve the usability of `proxmox_files` by allowing direct lookup of a file by name.

#### Example (hypothetical)

```hcl
data "proxmox_files" "base_image" {
  node_name    = var.node_name
  datastore_id = var.datastore_id
  content_type = "import"

  file_name = "noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.qcow2"
}
```

#### Expected behavior

* If the file exists → return it (e.g., expose `id`)
* If the file does not exist → return `null` (or empty result)

---

### Simplified Workflow with This Improvement

```hcl
resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file" "base_image" {
  count = data.proxmox_files.base_image.id == null ? 1 : 0

  node_name    = var.node_name
  datastore_id = var.datastore_id
  content_type = "import"

  url  = "https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
  file_name = "noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.qcow2"
}

resource "proxmox_virtual_environment_vm" "vm" {
  name      = "example-vm"
  node_name = var.node_name

  disk {
    datastore_id = var.datastore_id
    import_from      = data.proxmox_files.base_image.id != null
    ? data.proxmox_files.base_image.id
    : proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file.base_image[0].id
  }
}
```

---

### Benefits

* Eliminates manual filtering logic
* Reduces boilerplate significantly
* Keeps download responsibility in `proxmox_virtual_environment_download_file`
* Makes the workflow much more intuitive and readable
* Better aligns with common Terraform patterns

---

### Summary

While the provider already supports all required operations, the current user experience for "use existing or download if missing" is unnecessarily complex.

Allowing `proxmox_files` to query directly by file name would greatly simplify this workflow without changing existing responsibilities between data sources and resources.

Thank you for your work on this provider!

items.title: vm: delay reboot to work with guest-agent enabled cloud-images
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

If we deploy a VM, with guest-agent enabled cloud-image, and set `reboot=true` then the reboot command hangs with `qmp command 'guest-ping' failed - got timeout` and the VM is never rebooted due to proxmox issuing `guest-ping` command before the guest-agent service loads up in it.

nixos cloud-images support guest-agent but it takes some time to start the service.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Adding a 15-second delay to `reboot` command fixes this issues as qemu-guest-agent service is up when vm is booted. then the reboot command is issued to the VM and is successful.

**Additional context**

I've tested this with nixos cloud-image VM's and it works.  Below patch works for me.

https://github.com/HritwikSinghal/terraform-provider-proxmox/commit/de7d523fdd857e1821805a53ed3cbe615fa5250a

Can we fix this by adding a `reboot_delay` param?

items.body:
## Description

After the revert of disk re-import logic in PR #2401 (v0.89.0), there are two cleanup items left:

### 1. Orphaned code in `vmUpdateDiskLocationAndSize`

`proxmoxtf/resource/vm/vm.go` lines 6443-6446 still contain logic from PR #2150 that compares `ImportFrom` values and resets disk size to force a resize:

```go
// We need to resize the disk if the import source has changed.
if *oldDisk.ImportFrom != *diskNewEntries[oldIface].ImportFrom {
    *oldDisk.Size = 0
}
```

This code has no practical effect because `disk.Update()` (disk.go:630) no longer passes `ImportFrom` through to the update body. It should be removed to avoid confusion.

### 2. Misleading `import_from` schema description

The current description says:

> "The file id of a disk image to import from storage."

This doesn't mention that `import_from` is only used during initial disk creation and changes after creation are silently ignored. The description should be updated to make this clear.

## Context

- Discussion #2403 — decision to keep `import_from` as create-only
- PR #2150 — original re-import logic (merged in v0.88.0)
- PR #2401 — revert (merged in v0.89.0, closed #2385)
